Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement 2026-12-01 Medium

Dissecting the genetic architecture for maize prolificacy by combining QTL mapping and genome-wide association study.

This study dissects the genetic architecture of maize prolificacy (number of ears per plant) by combining QTL mapping in two recombinant inbred line populations with a genome-wide association study in an association panel, evaluated across multiple environments. The authors identify 13 QTLs and 8 quantitative trait nucleotides, including a stable locus (qP9-2) that harbors two genes linked to tissue differentiation. These findings provide candidate loci and genes for improving maize yield potential through breeding.

Non-coding RNA research 2026-12-01 Medium

Nanopore direct RNA sequencing reveals the 2'-O-methylation landscape and SNORD88B-guided FN1 modification in hepatocellular carcinoma.

This study uses nanopore direct RNA sequencing to map the internal 2'-O-methylation (Nm) landscape on mRNA in hepatocellular carcinoma, characterizing its distribution and biological functions. It further identifies C/D box snoRNAs, particularly SNORD88B, that guide Nm modification of the FN1 gene, providing a molecular basis for post-transcriptional regulation in HCC.

Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) 2026-11-20 Medium

ABAQS: A comprehensive scoring method for assessing genome annotation quality.

ABAQS introduces a comprehensive scoring method for evaluating the quality of genome annotations, addressing the growing need to assess accuracy and completeness of gene and protein models as genome resources expand. The method helps researchers select genomes with comparable annotation quality for comparative genomic analyses, preventing inconsistencies from undermining downstream studies.

Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) 2026-11-19 Medium

hlafactor: a tool for multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation.

hlafactor is a new software tool that consolidates multiple layers of HLA functional annotation—from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level properties like tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups—into a single resource. It addresses the current fragmentation of HLA functional data across publications and reference datasets, enabling integrated multi-layer analyses of this highly polymorphic immune region.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-19 Medium

DGIdb in 2026: an interoperable resource for the druggable genome.

DGIdb 2026 is an updated open-access database that aggregates and normalizes drug-gene interaction data from many sources, now adding three new datasets including the Molecular Oncology Almanac, PRISM Repurposing, and Broad Institute drug repurposing data. The release also improves programmatic access and local deployment options, making it easier for researchers to integrate druggable-genome information into their own pipelines.

The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD 2026-11-18 Medium

Multi-centre implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome test for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer.

This multi-centre study reports real-world implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome sequencing assay (SeqOne SomaHRD) for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer across four European laboratories. Tumours were classified HRD-positive based on a Genomic Instability score derived from large-scale genomic alterations and loss of heterozygosity, and/or pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants. The work demonstrates that low-coverage WGS-based HRD testing is scalable and feasible in routine clinical laboratory settings.

FEBS open bio 2026-11-18 Medium

DeGenRESOLVE: An offline GUI-based automated nanopore sequencing pipeline for viruses with custom rule-based indel and degeneracy resolution.

DeGenRESOLVE is an offline, GUI-based pipeline for analyzing amplicon-based Oxford Nanopore sequencing data from viruses when a reference genome is available. It automates the workflow and includes custom rule-based resolution of indels and degenerate bases, addressing the need for tools that work without internet access or advanced bioinformatics skills. The tool is aimed at laboratories with limited connectivity or expertise.

Cell reports methods 2026-11-17 Medium

Auditing the adversarial robustness of genomic foundation models with SafeGenes.

SafeGenes is an evaluation framework that stress-tests genomic foundation models (like ESM) used for clinical variant effect prediction. It introduces input-space attacks, a discrete SNV-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt backdoor, and shows that iterative attacks such as PGD can drop AUC by over 30 percentage points on cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets. The work highlights that these models are far less robust to adversarial perturbations than their clinical use might assume.

Functional & integrative genomics 2026-11-17 Medium

Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer.

This review discusses computational and experimental strategies for determining which non-coding genetic variants contribute to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. It highlights the challenge posed by the abundance of non-coding variants and the complexity of gene regulatory mechanisms, and outlines approaches to prioritize and functionally validate them.

Cancer science 2026-11-16 Medium

MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.

MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level in silico features with patient-level mutational context, addressing the limitation of existing tools that ignore clinical context. This integration aims to improve variant interpretation for comprehensive genomic profiling in precision oncology, particularly for variants lacking established consensus.

Molecular and cellular probes 2026-11-13 Medium

Pooled multiplex amplicon massive parallel sequencing for high-throughput confirmation of whole-genome sequencing potentially pathogenic variants in patients with parkinsonism.

The authors developed a pooled multiplex amplicon sequencing approach to confirm potentially pathogenic variants identified by whole-genome sequencing in patients with parkinsonism. By pooling DNA samples and using massively parallel sequencing of multiple amplicons, they provide a scalable alternative to Sanger sequencing for high-throughput variant validation. This method addresses the bottleneck of confirming large numbers of WGS variants in clinical and research settings.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-11-11 High

Detection of Maximal Exact Matches in Terabases of Genome Assemblies in Compressed Space and Sublinear Time.

The paper introduces a method for detecting maximal exact matches (MEMs) between all pairs of genome assemblies in large panels, operating directly on compressed data and in sublinear time. This enables scalable comparative genomics across terabase-scale pangenome collections, where pairwise MEM detection was previously computationally prohibitive.

PHI: a Galaxy-based workflow for reproducible prophage-host interaction analysis and standardized viral-genomics reporting.

PHI is a Galaxy-based workflow that integrates multiple computational tools into a single reproducible pipeline for identifying prophages in bacterial genomes and analyzing their interactions with hosts. It also standardizes viral-genomics reporting, making prophage analysis more accessible and consistent for researchers without extensive bioinformatics expertise.

Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P.

R2T2P is a computational platform that integrates transcriptomics and proteomics by combining genome-guided transcriptome assembly with translation and protein identification, plus a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. The authors applied it to a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, demonstrating its utility for integrative RNA-to-protein analysis.

A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans -regulatory architecture in the aging human brain.

The authors present TransMap, a computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Applied to the aging human brain, it produces a cell-type-resolved map of trans-regulatory architecture and constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that boost statistical power beyond individual trans-eGenes.

Computational biology and chemistry 2026-11-07 Medium

A computational tool to predict how new coronavirus variants evade antibody defenses.

RBD-Escape is a computational framework that predicts how combinations of mutations in the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain affect recognition by polyclonal neutralizing antibodies. It integrates deep mutational scanning data from 33 monoclonal antibodies across multiple studies into a unified model, aiming to forecast antibody evasion by new variants. The tool is designed to be transparent and experimentally grounded, supporting vaccine and therapeutic antibody development.

A Batch-Processing Pipeline for RNA-seq Gene Abundance Estimation.

The authors present a batch-processing pipeline for estimating gene abundance from RNA-seq data that handles heterogeneous datasets differing in library layout, read length, sequencing depth, and metadata quality. The pipeline is designed to be more accessible than existing workflow-manager-based approaches, reducing the need for advanced bioinformatics expertise or substantial computational infrastructure. It aims to enable consistent processing of multiple RNA-seq datasets for routine analyses.

gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cell quality control.

The authors present gcat and its_a_scam, two modular open-source tools for single-cell data processing and per-cell quality control. They argue that the trend toward monolithic, often proprietary end-to-end pipelines limits flexibility and reuse, and that composable tools better support non-standard analyses.

Royal Society open science 2026-11-04 Medium

Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.

This study compares the genomes of two ecologically similar plateau fishes (Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus) within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, and chromosome-scale synteny. The authors find contrasting candidate adaptive signatures between the two species despite their shared cold, hypoxic, high-UV plateau environments, suggesting that genomic responses to similar environmental pressures can diverge even among related fishes.

International journal of molecular sciences 2026-11-04 Medium

Topological Data Analysis Identifies Copy Number Variation Subtypes of Bulls Associated with Fertility.

This study applied topological data analysis (TDA) to genome-wide copy number variation region (CNVR) profiles from 88 bulls, grouping animals by CNV co-occurrence patterns rather than single-locus effects. The resulting CNV-based subgroups were associated with differences in insemination success rate, suggesting that combined CNV patterns capture fertility-relevant structure missed by conventional marginal association tests. It demonstrates TDA as a complementary approach for polygenic trait analysis in livestock.

medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences 2026-11-03 Medium

Variant Classification of a Non-Protein Coding Gene: ACMG/AMP Specifications for RMRP from the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel.

This work adapts the ACMG/AMP germline variant interpretation framework specifically for RMRP, a non-protein-coding RNA gene whose biallelic pathogenic variants cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia and can include severe combined immunodeficiency. The ClinGen SCID Variant Curation Expert Panel provides gene-specific specifications to address the challenges of classifying variants in a non-coding gene, extending the standard framework beyond its protein-coding origins.

Briefings in bioinformatics 2026-11-02 Medium

Correction of the cytosine deamination artifacts in FFPE-based sequencing experiments.

This paper systematically benchmarks seven computational tools designed to correct cytosine deamination artifacts (C>T/G>A substitutions) that arise in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue sequencing. The authors compare these methods across different tools and experimental conditions, addressing a gap where no prior systematic comparison existed. The work provides guidance on which correction approaches perform best for improving accuracy in FFPE-based next-generation sequencing analyses.

Horticulture research 2026-11-01 Medium

quarTeT after 3 years: toolkit updates and community insights for telomere-to-telomere genome assembly.

quarTeT, a toolkit for telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly, receives a major update improving all four of its modules: contig filtering in AssemblyMapper, a refactored join algorithm in GapFiller, enhanced telomere detection in TeloExplorer, and holocentric chromosome support in CentroMiner. The main program now offers configurable multithreading, broader version compatibility, and easier deployment via Bioconda, Docker, and Singularity. These updates make the widely used toolkit more robust and accessible for complete genome assembly projects.

Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.

Genome-wide association study of growth-related traits in mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi): identification of cross-trait associated loci and candidate genes using single-trait and multivariate linear mixed models.

cgMLST typing reproducibility is maintained across diverse whole-genome sequencing workflows in a multi-country HERA2 surveillance pilot.

This multi-country ring trial tested whether different laboratories' whole-genome sequencing workflows produce comparable cgMLST typing results for bacterial surveillance. Six labs in four European countries sequenced a standardized panel of 25 isolates across five public health-relevant species, and cgMLST-based interpretations remained reproducible despite workflow heterogeneity. The findings support the robustness of cgMLST typing for routine cross-laboratory surveillance.

Survey of viruses associated with the whitefly Bemisia tabaci in cucurbits in Georgia, United States.

This study surveyed the virome of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) collected from cucurbit crops in Georgia over two consecutive years using RNA sequencing. The authors characterized the diversity of viruses associated with this major agricultural pest, which could inform understanding of virus transmission potential and identify candidate viral biocontrol agents.
